Inability to practice optometry with reasonable skill and safety due to mental illness, physical illness, substance abuse, or communicable disease
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inability to practice optometry with reasonable skill and safety by reason of: (a) Mental illness; (b) Physical illness including, but not limited to, physical deterioration which adversely affects cognitive, motor or perceptive skills; (c) Habitual or excessive use or abuse of drugs defined in law as controlled substances, alcohol, or any other substances which impair ability; or (d) Having a communicable, contagious or infectious disease which endangers the health of patients.

definition_quote.value: The 'practice of optometry' means: (1) To engage in the profession of examining, testing, measuring, treating, correcting, developing or improving the human visual apparatus; (2) To display any sign, circular, advertisement or device offering to examine eyes, test eyes, fit glasses, adjust frames or prescribe lenses...; (3) To employ in the examination, diagnosis or treatment of another, any means, including the use of diagnostic pharmaceutical agents and pharmaceutical agents for therapeutic use...; (4) To remove superficial foreign bodies and to diagnose and treat superficial conditions of the eye and eyelid...; (5) To sell or offer for sale, otherwise than on prescription, any lens with spherical, prismatic or cylindrical power...; (6) To prescribe or adapt lenses, including contact lenses, exercises, orthoptics, vision therapy or other physical means to correct defects or adjust human vision...
definition_quote.quote: The "practice of optometry" means: (1) To engage in the profession of examining, testing, measuring, treating, correcting, developing or improving the human visual apparatus

drug_authority.value: Optometrists may use diagnostic pharmaceutical agents. A certificate from the state board of optometry is required to prescribe, administer, and dispense therapeutic pharmaceutical agents for treatment of conditions of the eye and/or eyelid, as approved and identified by board rules. Effective January 1, 2021, all licensees must be certified to use therapeutic pharmaceutical agents.
drug_authority.quote: The state board of optometry may, pursuant to rules adopted by it, issue a certificate to optometrists licensed in this state authorizing the optometrist to prescribe, administer and dispense such therapeutic pharmaceutical agents for the treatment of conditions of the eye and/or eyelid, as approved by the board of optometry and as identified in rules adopted by the board of optometry.
